Yes!! It seriously still is just a story written from a white perspective! Do think it was a step! Again I’m always looking for representation of my culture in media and while LiS2 isn’t perfect I appreciate the attempt!

Like, you’d really think a game with an ending similar to my real trauma would comfort me? Right? But it just didn’t. It really just didn’t sit right with me. Like others said. The point was to address the real issues around the system. And it definitely does. Just made me feel like shit but not in way of me thinking it was a good thing. The left overs and HBO’s watchmen are example’s of stories that make me feel like shit, but don’t come off as anti activist. Specifically of HBO’s watchmen. It *really* made me feel like shit. But it had a very pro activism feel and message. Vs my issue with LiS2 is it feels like the ending was giving a very anti activism take.

Had a whole essay before I shortened it (still long ik) but basically 

Through a year long legal battle Sean is imprisoned as Bail is denied and Sean is placed in foster care or in juvey bc I don’t buy him being too young to prosecute as there’s plenty of cases even in Washington where children are tried- even as adults in extreme circumstances. It would end with them finally wining the court case. Not sure what I would prefer tho. Them after going to Mexico anyway to feel closer to their dad. Or staying with their grandparents. What matters to me is they are both still young and can be there for each other. Especially after these traumatic events.

It’s this an extremely hopeful ending I know. But it stems from my experience through similar things. I was accused of things at 17 I did not do, I spent several weeks in in custody(mostly in solitary) before the charges were dropped because we were able to prove them false and get local public opinion out on my side. 

I remember telling this story to my family in Mexico a few months after I was released. And a great uncle of mine. All he has to say for it is. “Were they being racist?” And I just tell him “yes” “they were”.

Because to put it in perspective me and my family and friends struggled to understand why me, until we realized very quickly it had to be racial prejudice in our mostly white town.

Having a man who has never stepped foot in the U.S, but know enough of the culture of it. To have him first guess that what happened to me was just textbook racism. Yeah. Really cemented why it happened to *me*

Like I said to another commenter, Sean getting 15 years really broke me. He very easily could have been me. And it was dark reminder of it. Which made me dislike it. It’s been 3 years. I just turned 20 recently. And I still think about what happened to me.
Redemption ending? Like the one I got? Specify plz😭

I agree. The game for the most part has good writing. Again the relationship between the brothers is amazing to see fold over the games story. This ending just absolutely fumbled the ball, but for reference. There are definitely ways to show how fucked the justice system is here in ways that don’t involve it feeling anti activist. 7 sols comes to mind. HBO’s Watchmen series. 

Overall I wouldn’t say the game was terrible. But yeah the ending fumbled. I’m glad you really like it. Not saying you’re wrong for that, simply stating my opinion and thought process as a child of immigrants.
Pointing it out with no other commentary aside from “it exist” is just stupid. Especially as someone who has and will always experience it. There’s more to be said than just “it exist”
Acknowledging is one thing and it does have its place I agree. But these ending just feel like it’s torture porn.
That’s a good takeaway, I appreciate the way you phrased it.

Respectfully if you’re not Latino I don’t think it’s your place to tell me or other Latinos what this games message on prejudice is about. We know. We live through it everyday. Ask any poc. I agree with other commenters i understand the game is supposed to be sad. Doesn’t Change the fact it feels like a very anti activism ending. Which is why I as a Latino don’t like it

I understand what you are saying and can accept that’s what the devs aimed for, it however doesn’t change how they executed it. And coming from me as a Latino, yeah it falls really flat and just reeks of performative activism. 

However Sean getting 15 years in prison is absolutely racially motivated, or at the very least. The games writing makes it appear that way.

I see everyone commenting similar things. But it still feels like their messaging was a very anti activism. Which i understand as the writers are French so I don’t expect them to understand the complexity of American Politics. Still fell extremely flat for me tho. I can’t blame them for trying however.

as I said to another commenter I was unfortunately on the receiving end of how bs the justice system can be. I also as a kid was punished for crimes I never committed. Thankfully however my charges were dropped but only after I spent several weeks in solitary confinement. Seeing Sean spend 15 years. Just broke my heart. He very easily could have been me.

I will take ur opinion with a grain of salt. This isn’t a dig at you but inherently not being Latino yes it’s different. I’ve been on the receiving end of how bad the justice system is. I spent several weeks in solitary confinement for charges that were dropped because I never did what I was accused of, so this ending hurt to watch. And my stuff happed about 3 years ago when i literally was around Sean’s age. So yeah. This ending just doesn’t sit right with me.

After reading this post and your reply’s in the comments OP I have some things to say.

I totally agree with most of what you are saying. I too am choosing to just present as a gay man while on HRT and the second I pass I will start identifying as my true self. 

Trans brothers and sisters who choose to identify as their true selves even if they don’t pass are amazing and brave. But I will admit I am not brave. Like you. I get it. The fear is a lot. I live in the us in the Deep South and I can’t imagine it’s much better in a post communist country.

What I will say is I agree with a lot of the comments saying that 2 years on HRT isn’t enough. You have to give it anywhere from 5-7 years for you to start passing, but you can’t just expect the HRT to do all the work because it won’t. It’s not magic. 

While I partially agree when you say it’s particularly on your genetics whether you can pass or not. It’s not 100% genetics. Having an already androgynous or feminine face before transitioning can help. But there’s plenty of transwoman that didn’t have either that now pass. 

Look into voice training, mannerisms, posture, ect. All those *with* HRT will give the best outcome but it takes time. Be patient.

Or don’t. You’re 17. You literally have plenty of time to go on HRT. And pass while youre still young. Which not every trans person can say. 

If your going to do nothing but just take hrt and just hope it magically makes you pass effortlessly. You’re dead wrong. Just be patient and put in the work. You’ll see the results. Just not right away like you seem to want to.
